_comment: Single source of truth for which 'MAS Mapping' categories are in active Phase 1
scope -- for BOTH supply (AFD-Supply.xlsx) and demand (Demand.xlsx). Decided 2026-10-01:
only Full Stack and Front End are active; everything else is deferred to Phase 2.
Flip a category's status to 'active' to bring it into scope -- but read
demand-supply-mapping-requirements.md's 'MAS Mapping scoping' section first: activating a
category here does NOT by itself produce correct matches. It only stops this gate from
excluding the category's rows; classify_demand_row()/classify_supply_row() in engine.py
still have no dedicated persona or supply pool for Tpm/Testing/Polyglot/etc, so an activated
category's skill-cluster text would just get forced into whichever of Fullstack
Java/Fullstack .NET/Frontend it happens to resemble -- the same category-mismatch problem
this gate exists to prevent. Real activation = flip this file AND build that category's
persona + supply pool + matching rules.
KEEP THIS FILE AND THE JAVA WEB APP'S V7__mas_mapping_categories.sql SEED DATA IDENTICAL.
This project runs two parallel implementations (this CLI and bench-match-webapp) during a
build -> parallel-run -> sunset period; the Java side has no equivalent JSON file (it reads
its own DB table instead), so there is no automatic sync -- whoever changes one must change
the other by hand, the same lesson already learned the hard way from the AFD Status
case-sensitivity bug (2026-09-30), which was fixed in Python and nearly forgotten on the
Java side until it was flagged explicitly.
A category not listed here defaults to inactive (the safe default) -- see
load_mas_mapping_scope() in classify_inputs.py.

categories.note: Technical Project Management -- not an engineering role; not a skill-confidence question like the others below
